title: India's Kharif Rice Sowing Hits Record 38 Million Hectares This Season

headline: Millet Food Products — FPOs Earn ₹2 Crore by Processing Jowar into Cookies and Pasta
summary: A Farmer Producer Organisation in Solapur, Maharashtra is generating ₹2 crore annual revenue by processing sorghum (jowar) into cookies, pasta, breakfast cereals, and flour for urban health food chains. Jowar is gluten-free and high in iron, making it popular among health-conscious consumers. FPOs can access NHB food processing equipment subsidy at 50%. NABARD offers ₹50 lakh low-interest loan for food processing machinery.
keywords: millets, jowar, sorghum, food processing, FPO, market, Maharashtra, income

title: Rice Stubble to Bio-CNG — UP Plant Converts Paddy Waste into Compressed Gas
headline: Rice Stubble to Bio-CNG — UP Plant Converts Paddy Waste into Compressed Gas
summary: A new bio-CNG plant in Sangrur, Punjab, converts paddy stubble that was previously burned into compressed natural gas used as vehicle fuel. Farmers are paid ₹1,500-2,000 per acre for their stubble instead of burning it. The plant processes 200 tonnes of stubble per day. This gives farmers extra income, reduces air pollution, and produces fertilizer-quality digestate as byproduct. Six more plants are planned in UP.
keywords: rice, paddy, stubble, bio-CNG, technology, Punjab, renewable energy, income

title: Crop Area Insurance — Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Enrolment for Kharif Closes August 31
headline: Crop Area Insurance — Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Enrolment for Kharif Closes August 31
summary: Farmers who have not yet enrolled in PMFBY for kharif 2026 must do so before August 31 to be eligible for crop loss compensation. Enrol through your crop loan bank or visit any Common Service Centre with land records, Aadhaar, and crop sowing declaration. Premium is only 2% for kharif food crops and oilseeds. Farmers affected by current floods in Bihar, Assam, and WB are especially advised to enrol immediately.
keywords: crop insurance, PMFBY, Fasal Bima, kharif, government scheme, flood, subsidy

title: Wheat Flour Price — Atta at ₹35/Kg Due to Supply Pressure from Imports
headline: Wheat Flour Price — Atta at ₹35/Kg Due to Supply Pressure from Imports
summary: Retail atta (wheat flour) prices have eased to ₹32-35 per kg after government permitted selective wheat imports from Australia and Russia. Wholesale wheat prices at mandis have also softened to ₹2,450 per quintal. Farmers with stored wheat are advised to sell now at current prices as analysts expect further softening. NAFED and FCI are also releasing wheat stocks from buffer to control retail prices.
keywords: wheat, flour, atta, price, market, FCI, imports, mandi

title: Jamun and Amla Cultivation — Medicinal Fruit Farming Earns ₹3 Lakh/Acre
headline: Jamun and Amla Cultivation — Medicinal Fruit Farming Earns ₹3 Lakh/Acre
summary: Medicinal fruit cultivation of Jamun (Java Plum) and Amla (Indian Gooseberry) can earn farmers ₹2.5-3.5 lakh per acre per year in UP and MP. Both crops are drought-hardy, require minimal inputs, and have growing urban demand for their health benefits. NMPB (National Medicinal Plants Board) provides 30% subsidy on planting material. Jamun juice fetches ₹120 per litre and amla powder ₹200 per kg in organic markets.
keywords: jamun, amla, fruits, medicinal plants, organic, income, cultivation

title: Maize Ethanol — UP Farmers Get ₹3,200/Quintal Maize Contract from Ethanol Plant
headline: Maize Ethanol — UP Farmers Get ₹3,200/Quintal Maize Contract from Ethanol Plant
summary: An ethanol distillery in Meerut, UP, has signed direct purchase contracts with 500 maize farmers at ₹3,200 per quintal, which is above market price of ₹2,800. The plant uses maize starch to produce ethanol for blending in petrol under the 20% ethanol blending programme. Farmers benefit from assured market and predictable price. Contract requires delivery of dry maize at 14% moisture content directly at distillery gate.
keywords: maize, corn, ethanol, price, market, contract, UP, Uttar Pradesh

title: Soil Carbon Sequestration — Zero Budget Natural Farming Spreads to 5 Lakh Acres in AP
headline: Soil Carbon Sequestration — Zero Budget Natural Farming Spreads to 5 Lakh Acres in AP
summary: Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF), which uses Jeevamrit (fermented cow dung solution), Ghanajeevamrit, and mulching, has expanded to 5 lakh acres in Andhra Pradesh. Farmers spend ₹0 on synthetic inputs and earn higher prices selling organic certified produce. Average farm income increased by 25-30% in the 4th and 5th year after transitioning. ZBNF also restores soil biology, improves water retention, and reduces dependency on purchased inputs.
keywords: organic farming, zero budget, natural farming, Andhra Pradesh, soil, Jeevamrit

title: Kisan Rail — ₹50/Kg Freight Rate for Fresh Vegetables from Nashik to Delhi
headline: Kisan Rail — ₹50/Kg Freight Rate for Fresh Vegetables from Nashik to Delhi
summary: Indian Railways' Kisan Rail service now connects 72 source agriculture hubs to distant consumption markets at subsidised freight rates of ₹50 per kg for fresh vegetables. Nashik farmers can send onion, tomato, and grapes to Delhi in 16 hours. The service provides refrigerated vans to maintain freshness. Farmers can book space online 24 hours before departure. 50% freight subsidy is available for FPO groups.
keywords: Kisan Rail, vegetables, transport, market, Nashik, Maharashtra, logistics

title: Agri Budget 2026-27 — ₹1.52 Lakh Crore Allocated for Agriculture and Allied Sectors
headline: Agri Budget 2026-27 — ₹1.52 Lakh Crore Allocated for Agriculture and Allied Sectors
summary: The Union Budget 2026-27 has allocated ₹1.52 lakh crore for agriculture and allied sectors, the highest ever. Key highlights include ₹5 lakh PM Kisan allocation, ₹20,000 crore for PM Sinchai Yojana irrigation, ₹10,000 crore for agricultural infrastructure fund, and ₹2,500 crore for digital agriculture. Agricultural R&D receives ₹15,000 crore boost with focus on climate-resilient crop varieties. Farmer income is targeted to double by 2030.
keywords: budget, agriculture, government scheme, PM Kisan, allocation, farmer income
